errors.english: must refrain from knotting the edge of the lower robe
errors.why: The rule (whose stated purpose is keeping the private parts covered) prescribes tying the edge of the lower robe in a knot when climbing a ladder or sleeping by day, not refraining from it.

errors.english: Nor repeatedly carry them on the shoulders, head, or waist.
errors.why: As the commentary's ཁུར་ཡང་དུ་ཟིན་ཀྱང་ shows, ཡང་ here means 'light' (even a light load is not to be carried on shoulder, head or waist), not 'repeatedly'; the commentary rendering also adds 'repeatedly'.

note: A careful rendering of the Vinaya verses and commentary on grooming, the barber's sequence and deportment, with one probable inversion of the robe-knot rule.

errors.english: incurs the fault of undermining the intrinsic nature of phenomena
errors.why: ཆོས here is the property (dharma) of the thesis; the fault is that the very nature of the property to be proved (being made by another) is refuted, not anything about 'phenomena'.

fix.find: incurs the fault of undermining the intrinsic nature of phenomena
fix.replace: incurs the fault that the very nature of the property [to be proved] is refuted

errors.english: the elliptical remainder of the phrase is: "If this is other than that, and if that is other than this."
errors.why: The Tibetan says the quoted lines 'because those others made this...' are the remainder (continuation) of the conditional 'if this is other than that...', not the reverse.

note: The argument against suffering made by another is followed accurately; one logical term is flattened and the verse-completion relation is inverted.

errors.english: is an imputation of the cause to the result
errors.why: The figure is designating the cause by the name of the result (kāraṇe kāryopacāra), i.e. imputing the result onto the cause.

note: A sound rendering of the definition of cittotpāda and the eight abhisamayas, with the direction of the metonymy reversed.

errors.english: If sin were the cause or the pervasive quality of heaviness
errors.why: ཁྱབ་བྱ is the pervaded (vyāpya), not the pervader; the doubt is that sin is the cause of heaviness or what is pervaded by it, so that lightness opposes the effect or the pervader.

fix.find: If sin were the cause or the pervasive quality of heaviness
fix.replace: If sin were the cause of heaviness or what is pervaded by it

errors.english: it is in contradiction with the abandonment of heaviness, not with the sin itself
errors.why: Because consecration removes heaviness, it is contrary to heaviness (not to sin); the English makes it contrary to the removal of heaviness.

note: The Pramāṇa critique of consecration removing sin is broadly followed, but the vyāpya/vyāpaka logic and one contrariety are garbled.

errors.english: this is the sixty-first branch, entitled *The Story of the Farmer*
errors.why: This is the closing colophon of the preceding (61st) story; presented as a title it makes the following Suprabuddha story look like the Farmer story.

note: The Kalpalatā verses are rendered faithfully from the Tibetan; only the colophon is framed as a heading for what follows.
A faithful word-commentary rendering on the Madhyamaka reply to Cittamātra about form and mind; nothing of substance to change.

errors.why: བདག་གི་དངོས་པོ is ātmabhāva, the bodhisattva's body or embodiment (the mind-made body under discussion), not a 'self-entity'.
བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་མ is the Bhagavatī, i.e. the Prajñāpāramitā sūtra cited as a source, not the Buddha as speaker.

fix.replace: In the Bhagavatī [Prajñāpāramitā] it is also said

errors.english: yet it is not a worldly emanation
errors.why: The Tibetan says the mind-made body is to be seen as like an emanation but is not an emanation; 'worldly' is added.

errors.english: however, this is not a birth within the stainless sphere
errors.why: The point is that what ceases is birth in the three realms, not birth in the uncontaminated sphere; the English garbles this into a statement about what kind of birth 'this' is.

note: Generally followable, but ātmabhāva and the Bhagavatī citation are mistranslated and the argument about birth in the uncontaminated sphere is blurred.

errors.english: it would be the (Vedavadin) one who upholds the Vedas who is established by intrinsic nature
errors.why: རིག་བྱེད་པ here is the Vedic statement/meaning (vaidika), which the opponent claims is self-established; it is not a person who upholds the Vedas.

fix.find: it would be the (Vedavadin) one who upholds the Vedas who is established by intrinsic nature
fix.replace: it is that the Vedic [statement] is established by its own nature

errors.english: no distinction is seen between the followers of the (Veda) and the worldly ones
errors.why: The comparison is between Vedic and worldly statements, not between Veda followers and worldly people (the same slip recurs in 'the worldly ones and the (Veda) followers').
In this argument དམ་བཅས་པ is the convention/stipulation (samaya) laid down by a powerful person, which is what makes mantras effective, not a 'vow'.

note: The argument that Vedic and worldly speech cannot be distinguished as unauthored is followed, but Vedic statements are repeatedly turned into Vedic persons.

errors.english: the claim that whatever exists is a qualifier of the subject is incorrect
errors.why: The rejected claim is that what is present [in the formulation] is the qualifier of the subject, not that 'whatever exists' is such a qualifier.

note: A good rendering of the grammatical debate over the ablative in udāharaṇasādharmyāt; one clause misconstrued.

errors.why: གནོད་པ་ཅན་གྱི་ཚད་མ is bādhakapramāṇa, the invalidating (refuting) means of valid cognition.
འཁྲུལ་པ here is logical deviation (vyabhicāra) of the reason: how could [the reason] deviate so that something is both existent and permanent.

note: The momentariness argument and the opponent's doubt about anvaya/vyatireka are rendered accurately; two logical terms are off.
